document: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI)
article_or_section: Article 10(1)-(4), (6) (Chapter III, Section 2) – Data and data governance; read with Article 4a(1)
implementation_notes: Not assessed: legislative obligation, not a policy commitment. Timing is recorded in applicability_status. Check separately whether harmonised standards supporting this article have been published. APPLICABILITY: from 2 Dec 2027 (Art. 6(2)/Annex III systems) or 2 Aug 2028 (Art. 6(1)/Annex I systems), per Art. 113 as amended. Provider duty; not applicable to AI systems that are not high-risk (Art. 4a(2) permission does extend to them).
verification_notes: CODING DECISION: Art. 10 is fundamentally a data governance provision, even though some of its requirements relate to risk mitigation. It is coded under Risk Assessment for now because its core operative elements, bias examination (Art. 10(2)(f)), bias detection, prevention and mitigation (Art. 10(2)(g)) and identification of data gaps (Art. 10(2)(h)), are risk identification and mitigation functions. Secondary dimension: Data Governance (see secondary_dimension; candidate sixth dimension for the codebook). A further link to Safety and Testing (quality of testing data sets) is noted but not coded. Single record, no double count. AMENDMENT: Reg. (EU) 2026/1744 amended Art. 10(1) (M1 marker) so the quality criteria now refer to paras 2, 3 and 4 and to Art. 4a(1) instead of paras 2 to 5. It also deleted Art. 10(5) and moved the special-category data rule into new Art. 4a (cons. p. 12). The coded exact_text (opening of Art. 10(2)) appears unamended. PERMISSION vs OBLIGATION: Art. 4a(1) PERMITS providers of high-risk AI systems, exceptionally and where strictly necessary, to process special categories of personal data for the bias detection and correction required by Art. 10(2)(f)-(g), subject to cumulative safeguards. Art. 4a(2) extends that permission to providers and deployers of other AI systems and models and to deployers of high-risk systems, and expressly states that it does not create any obligation to conduct bias detection and correction. So the DUTY to examine and mitigate bias comes from Art. 10(2)(f)-(g) and binds high-risk providers only, while Art. 4a is an enabling permission, not an obligation, and is not coded as a separate mandatory record. Must be read alongside the GDPR (Art. 1(2)(g) as amended is without prejudice to Art. 4a). APPLICATION DATE: as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744, Art. 113 (cons. p. 128; OJ p. 123) applies Chapter III high-risk obligations from 2 Dec 2027 for systems classified under Art. 6(2) and Annex III, and from 2 Aug 2028 for systems classified under Art. 6(1) and Annex I (originally 2 Aug 2026 and 2 Aug 2027 respectively). As of Nov 2026 the obligation is binding law but not yet applicable. Re-check consolidated pages in your own downloaded copy. CODING CHANGE 2026-11-26: secondary dimension changed from 'Data Governance' (not a framework dimension) to 'Safety and Testing'; data governance remains a candidate sixth dimension.

implementation_notes: COMMITMENT: voluntary transparency reports by developers/deployers; MeitY 'may publish a schedule' for compliance within 9-12 months (PDF p. 33).
